verses.sanskrit:
भीष्म उवाच।
              तमहं स्मयन्निव रणे प्रत्यभाषं व्यवस्थितम्। भूमिष्ठं नोत्सहे योद्धुं भवन्तं रथमास्थितः ॥१॥
verses.english: Bhishma said Laughingly I said to him who stood there for battle: Myself riding on a chariot I do not venture to fight with you who are on the ground.

verses.sanskrit: आरोह स्यन्दनं वीर कवचं च महाभुज। बधान समरे राम यदि योद्धुं मयेच्छसि ॥२॥
verses.english: Mount on a chariot, O hero, and adjust your coat of mail, O you of long arms if, O Rama, you desire to fight with me.

verses.sanskrit: ततो मामब्रवीद्रामः स्मयमानो रणाजिरे। रथो मे मेदिनी भीष्म वाहा वेदाः सदश्ववत् ॥३॥
verses.english: Then did Rama say to me laughingly in the field of battle: "The earth is chariot, O Bhishma, and the Vedas carry me like good horses.

verses.sanskrit: सुतश्च मातरिश्वा वै कवचं वेदमातरः। सुसंवीतो रणे ताभिर्योत्स्येऽहं कुरुनन्दन ॥४॥
verses.english: The wind is my driver, and the mothers of the Vedas (Gayatri, Savitri and Sarasvati) constitute my coat of mail. Well protected by these, in battle, I shall fight, O you delighter of the Kurus."

verses.sanskrit: एवं ब्रुवाणो गान्धारे रामो मां सत्यविक्रमः। शरव्रातेन महता सर्वतः प्रत्यवारयत् ॥५॥
verses.english: Saying thus, O son of Gandhari, Rama of true prowess covered me on all sides with a thick shower of arrows.

verses.sanskrit: ततोऽपश्यं जामदग्न्यं रथमध्ये व्यवस्थितम्। सर्वायुधवरे श्रीमत्यद्भुतोपमदर्शने ॥६॥
verses.english: Then did I see the son of Jamadagni seated on a car holding all the principal weapons, endued with beauty and appearing wonderful to the sight.

verses.sanskrit: मनसा विहिते पुण्ये विस्तीर्णे नगरोपमे। दिव्याश्वयुजि सन्नद्धे काञ्चनेन विभूषिते ॥७॥
verses.english: The car was created by his will force and was like a holy and spacious city with celestial horses yoked to it and well protected and ornamented with gold.

verses.sanskrit: कवचेन महाबाहो सोमार्ककृतलक्ष्मणा। धनुर्धरो बद्धतूणो बद्धगोधाङ्गुलित्रवान् ॥८॥
verses.english: He was also clad in a coat of mail, O you of long arms, looking like the sun and moon, wielding a bow furnished with a quiver and with his fingers protected by gloves.

verses.sanskrit: सारथ्यं कृतवांस्तत्र युयुत्सोरकृतव्रणः। सखा वेदविदत्यन्तं दयितो भार्गवस्य ह ॥९॥
verses.english: Akritavrana, desirous of fighting, performed the office of the charioteer in that battle. He was the dear friend of that descendant Bhrigu and very well versed in Vedas.

verses.sanskrit: आह्वयानः स मां युद्धे मनो हर्षयतीव मे। पुनः पुनरभिक्रोशन्नभियाहीति भार्गवः ॥१०॥
verses.english: When he challenged me to fight my heart was very much pleased. The descendant of Bhrigu said to me again and again "come, come.”

verses.sanskrit: तमादित्यमिवोद्यन्तमनाधृष्यं महाबलम्। क्षत्रियान्तकरं राममेकमेकः समासदम् ॥११॥
verses.english: Then did I approach him who was blazing like the sun, incapable of being vanquished and endued with great strength. Alone I approached Rama, the exterminator of the Kshatriya race.

verses.sanskrit: ततोऽहं बाणपातेषु त्रिषु वाहान्निगृह्य वै। अवतीर्य धनुर्न्यस्य पदातिरृषिसत्तमम् ॥१२॥
verses.english: After receiving three showers of arrows I stopped my horses and dismounting and putting aside my bow, I went on foot to that best among the Rishis.

verses.sanskrit: अभ्यागच्छं तदा राममर्चिष्यन् द्विजसत्तमम्। अभिवाद्य चैनं विधिवद‌ब्रुवं वाक्यमुत्तमम् ॥१३॥
verses.english: And coming before him I worshipped Rama the best among the twice born and after saluting him addressed him suitably in these excellent words.

verses.sanskrit: योत्स्ये त्वया रणे राम सदृशेनाधिकेन वा। गुरुणा धर्मशीलेन जयमाशास्व मे विभो ॥१४॥
verses.english: Whether you are equal to me or superior I shall fight with you, my lord, though you are my virtuous preceptor. Bless me that I may obtain victory.

verses.sanskrit:
राम उवाच।
              एवमेतत् कुरुश्रेष्ठ कर्तव्यं भूतिमिच्छता। धर्मो ह्येष महाबाहो विशिष्टैः सह युध्यताम् ॥१५॥
verses.english: Rama said O foremost among the Kurus, such should be done by one who desires prosperity. It is virtuous, O you of long arms, to fight with those that are well known.

verses.sanskrit: शपेयं त्वां न चेदेवमागच्छेया विशांपते। युध्यस्व त्वं रणे यत्तो धैर्यमालम्ब्य कौरव ॥१६॥
verses.english: If, O lord of the universe, you had not thus come to me I would have cursed you; fight you in battle with patience, O son of Kuru.

verses.sanskrit: न तु ते जयमाशासे त्वां विजेतुमहं स्थितः। गच्छ युध्यस्व धर्मेण प्रीतोऽस्मि चरितेन ते ॥१७॥
verses.english: I cannot bless you for victory, for I myself am standing here to vanquish you Go, fight fairly, I am pleased with your conduct.

verses.sanskrit: ततोऽहं तं नमस्कृत्य रथमारुह्य सत्वरः। प्राध्मापयं रणे शङ्खं पुनर्हेमपरिष्कृतम् ॥१८॥
verses.english: Then did I, after saluting him, quickly mount my chariot and again blew loudly my conch in the field of battle, a conch set with gold.
verses.bhavadeepa: न तु ते जयमाशासे इत्युक्तिर्भूतिमिच्छता त्वया प्रागेव मदभिवंदनस्य जयहेतोः कृतत्वादिति भावः । तच्चैवमेतत्कुरुश्रेष्ठ कर्तव्यं भूतिमिच्छतेत्यनेन सूचितम् ॥१७॥

verses.sanskrit: ततो युद्धं समभवन्मम तस्य च भारत। दिवसान् सुबहून् राजन् परस्परजिगीषया ॥१९॥
verses.english: Then did the fight take place between myself and him, O Bharata for a great many days, O king, during which each was desirous of vanquishing the other.

verses.sanskrit: स मे तस्मिन् रणे पूर्वं प्राहरत् कङ्कपत्रिभिः। षष्ट्या शतैश्च नवभिः शराणां नतपर्वणाम् ॥२०॥
verses.english: In the battle, he first struck me with straight arrows with wings of vulture to the number of six hundred and nine.

verses.sanskrit: चत्वारस्तेन मे वाहाः सुतश्चैव विशाम्पते। प्रतिरुद्धास्तथैवाहं समरे दंशितः स्थितः ॥२१॥
verses.english: By that shower, my four horses as also my chariot, O lord of the universe, completely covered; but clad in a coat of mail, I myself remained calm.

verses.sanskrit: नमस्कृत्य च देवेभ्यो ब्राह्मणेभ्यो विशेषतः। तमहं स्मयन्निव रणे प्रत्यभाषं व्यवस्थितम् ॥२२॥
verses.english: Bowing to the gods and especially to the Brahmanas I laughingly said to him who was standing there for battle. were

verses.sanskrit: आचार्यता मानिता मे निर्मर्यादे ह्यपि त्वयि। भूयश्च शृणु मे ब्रह्मन् सम्पदं धर्मसंग्रहे ॥२३॥
verses.english: I have shown sufficient respect to yourself as a preceptor, though you have paid little regard to me. Listen again, O Brahmana, to what should be done if you want to acquire virtue.

verses.sanskrit: ये ते वेदाः शरीरस्था ब्राह्मण्यं यच्च ते महत्। तपश्च ते महत्तप्तं न तेभ्यः प्रहराम्यहम् ॥२४॥
verses.english: The Vedas that are in your body and the great spirit of Brahma that is there and the great asceticism practiced by you, I do not strike at.

verses.sanskrit: प्रहारे क्षत्रधर्मस्य यं राम त्वं समाश्रितः। ब्राह्मणः क्षत्रियत्वं हि याति शस्त्रसमुद्यमात् ॥२५॥
verses.english: I shall strike at your Kshatriya-hood since, O Rama, you have adopted the life of a Kshatriya; a Brahmana becomes a Kshatriya owing to his taking up arms.

verses.sanskrit: पश्य मे धनुषो वीर्यं पश्य बाह्वोर्बलं मम। एष ते कार्मुकं वीर छिनद्मि निशितेषुणा ॥२६॥
verses.english: Behold now the strength of my bow; and behold the might of my arms. O hero, I shall cut asunder this bow of yours by my arrows.

verses.sanskrit: तस्याहं निशितं भल्लं चिक्षेप भरतर्षभ। तेनास्य धनुषः कोटिं छित्वा भूमावपातयम् ॥२७॥
verses.english: Then did I hurl towards him a broad headed arrow and by it his bow broke into a million pieces and fell to the ground.

verses.sanskrit: तथैव च पृषत्कानां शतानि नतपर्वणाम्। चिक्षेप कङ्कपत्राणां जामदग्न्यरथं प्रति ॥२८॥
verses.english: In the same way, I shot a hundred arrows furnished with the wings of a vulture on the son of Jamadagni.

verses.sanskrit: काये विषक्तास्तु तदा वायुना समुदीरिताः। चेलुः क्षरन्तो रुधिरं नागा इव च ते शराः ॥२९॥
verses.english: Piercing through his body and carried along by the wind the arrows sped along dropping blood and acting like serpents.

verses.sanskrit: क्षतजोक्षितसर्वाङ्गः क्षरन् स रुधिरं रणे। बभौ रामस्तदा राजन् मेरुर्धातुमिवोत्सृजन् ॥३०॥
verses.english: Rama, then with all his body wondered and covered all over with blood, shone in battle like a mountain dropping melted metal.

verses.sanskrit: हेमन्तान्तेऽशोक इव रक्तस्तबकमण्डितः। बभौ रामस्तथा राजन् प्रफुल्ल इव किंशुकः ॥३१॥
verses.english: He looked like the Ashoka tree, at the end of winter, covered with bunches of red flowers or, O king, like the Kinshuka tree when laden with flowers.

verses.sanskrit: ततोऽन्यद्धनुरादाय रामः क्रोधसमन्वितः। हेमपुङ्खान् सुनिशितान् शरांस्तान् हि ववर्ष सः ॥३२॥
verses.english: Then did Rama, wrathfully taking up another bow, shoot forth arrows well sharpened and furnished with golden wings.

verses.sanskrit: ते समासाद्य मां रौद्रा बहुधा मर्मभेदिनः। अकम्पयन्महावेगाः सर्पानलविषोपमाः ॥३३॥
verses.english: Those fierce arrows, which were like flames and poisonous serpents coming from several sides, caused me to tremble at their great force and pierced my very vitals.

verses.sanskrit: तमहं समवष्टभ्य पुनरात्मानमाहवे। शतसंख्यैः शरैः क्रुद्धस्तदा राममवाकिरम् ॥३४॥
verses.english: Then did I, with wrath, shoot on Rama arrows, hundred in number after summoning all my patience and addressing myself to battle.

verses.sanskrit: स तैरग्न्यर्कसङ्काशैः शरैराशीविषोपमैः। शितैरभ्यर्दितो रामो मन्दचेता इवाभवत् ॥३५॥
verses.english: Rama, struck with those arrows which were like fire or the sun and like poisonous snakes, became like one senseless.

verses.sanskrit: ततोऽहं कृपयाऽऽविष्टो विष्टभ्यात्मानमात्मना। धिग्धिगित्यबुवं युद्धं क्षत्रधर्मं च भारत ॥३६॥
verses.english: Then was I filled with pity and stopped of my own will and said: "Fie, fie on battle and on Kshatriya practices." O Bharata.

verses.sanskrit: असकृच्चाब्रुवं राजन् शोकवेगपरिप्लुतः। अहो बत कृतं पापं मयेदं क्षत्रधर्मणा ॥३७॥
verses.english: Being filled with grief I said, “I am a vicious man and what sins have been committed by me for observing the duties of a Kshatriya. one

verses.sanskrit: गुरुर्द्विजातिर्धर्मात्मा यदेवं पीडितः शरैः। ततो न प्राहरं भूयो जामदग्न्याय भारत ॥३८॥
verses.english: For I have hurt with my arrows my preceptor who is a Brahmana of a virtuous soul. After that O Bharata I did not strike at Jamadagni's son.

verses.sanskrit: अथावताप्य पृथिवीं पूषा दिवससंक्षये। जगामास्तं सहस्त्रांशुस्ततो युद्धमुपारमत् ॥३९॥
verses.english: At this time, at the end of day, the sun of a thousand rays after heating the earth, went to his rooms and the fight too closed for the day.
